_comment: ID ledger for the MOBA generators -- read by apps/moba/id_alloc.py. Every custom ID this fork assigns belongs to exactly one owner's block. Two owners must NEVER share a block: generators window-clear their blocks, so an overlap lets one wipe the other's rows. Namespaces are independent -- waypoint_data 900206 and creature_template 900206 are unrelated ids and both legal. A namespace names a table; the id is that table's primary key.

store.note: creature.guid, NOT an entry. gen_store.py spawns shopkeepers with guid == entry so the two read together, which is why these numbers match the creature_template/store block -- they are still unrelated ids in unrelated namespaces. The only static spawn rows the fork owns; towers, creeps, neutrals and domes are spawned from C++ and have no rows here.
hand-assigned in maps/*/store_config.yaml under shopkeeper.teams; the generated SQL clears the whole block

towers.note: auto-assigned; the record is maps/*/tower_config.lock.json. 6 of 10 used -- map #2 overflows this block, and the right second-block size is knowable then, not now.

base_dome.note: hand-assigned in maps/*/base_config.yaml under spawn.dome; the generated SQL clears the whole block

item_copies.note: NOT a dense window: a copy's entry is its SOURCE entry + 900000, so this block is a sparse mirror of the whole stock item space. Nothing allocates here and there is nothing to enumerate -- the block exists so a future allocator cannot wander in. The client-patch drop-item copies will land here too, under the same offset.

creep_paths.note: auto-assigned in forward/reverse pairs; the record is maps/*/lane_config.lock.json. Mirrors lane_config.yaml's id_range, which stays the generator's own input until step 3 -- a second bundle declaring a different id_range would diverge from this block until then.
